exam_name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: A workload needs the cheapest model that still meets a 92 percent accuracy bar on a domain benchmark. What selection process is correct?

options.A: Measure each candidate on the domain benchmark, then choose the lowest-cost model that clears the bar with margin
options.B: Pick the largest available model for safety
options.C: Pick the cheapest model without testing

questions.explanation: Empirical benchmark scores dominate parameter counts for task fit, and cost minimisation applies only among models that clear the bar.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Why does few-shot example selection matter more than example count for a classification task?

options.A: Representative and diverse examples define the decision boundary; redundant examples add tokens without new signal
options.B: More examples always improve accuracy linearly
options.D: Count is the only factor that matters

questions.explanation: A few well-chosen examples covering the boundary and edge cases outperform many near-duplicates.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: A prompt works on short inputs but degrades on long ones. What is the most likely mechanism?

options.A: Positional effects such as lost-in-the-middle dilute attention to key instructions placed centrally
options.B: The model refuses long inputs entirely

questions.explanation: Attention dilution over long contexts means critical instructions should be repeated or placed where they are most attended.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which technique best constrains a model to a fixed output vocabulary for a routing task?

options.A: Constrained decoding or a post-generation validator with a repair step, guided by an explicit enumeration of allowed values

questions.explanation: Enumerating the allowed labels plus decoding constraints or validation eliminates out-of-vocabulary outputs that prompts alone cannot.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What is the risk of optimising a prompt solely against a small golden dataset?

options.A: Overfitting to those cases, producing a brittle prompt that fails on real-world variation

questions.explanation: A narrow evaluation set rewards prompts tuned to its quirks; held-out diversity is required to confirm robustness.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: When should a team prefer fine-tuning over prompt engineering for a style requirement?

options.A: When the style must be applied consistently across many prompts and the engineering overhead of repeating it exceeds the tuning cost
options.C: Prompt engineering can never express style

questions.explanation: Persistent behavioural traits amortise tuning cost across all future prompts, whereas prompt repetition pays the token cost forever.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does a model's context window determine for a summarisation pipeline?

options.A: The maximum input plus output tokens per call, which dictates the chunking and map-reduce strategy
options.B: The number of users that can call it
options.C: The storage size of the model weights

questions.explanation: Window size is a hard per-call budget, so documents exceeding it must be processed hierarchically.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Why run prompt evaluations at temperature zero when comparing candidates?

options.A: Deterministic outputs isolate prompt effects from sampling noise
options.B: Zero temperature always gives the best quality
options.C: Sampling must never be used in production
options.D: Temperature zero doubles the context window

questions.explanation: Fixing decoding to greedy removes randomness so observed differences can be attributed to the prompt change.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: A chain-of-thought prompt improves accuracy but doubles latency. What is the correct trade-off analysis?

options.A: Compare the accuracy gain against the latency budget and consider distilling the reasoning into the final prompt or a smaller model
options.B: Always keep the longest reasoning chain
options.D: Latency is irrelevant for accuracy tasks

questions.explanation: Reasoning traces cost tokens and time, so the gain must justify the budget, with distillation as the standard mitigation.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which evidence best supports choosing one foundation model over another for production?

options.A: Head-to-head evaluation on production-representative tasks with cost and latency measured alongside quality

questions.explanation: Task-specific quality plus operational cost and latency is the only basis that predicts production fitness.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What is the principal failure mode of stuffing an entire policy manual into a prompt for compliance checking?

options.A: The model may attend to irrelevant sections and miss the applicable rule, while token cost balloons
options.D: Longer prompts are always more accurate

questions.explanation: Retrieval of the relevant rule followed by focused reasoning outperforms dumping the whole manual into context.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A Bedrock knowledge base returns stale answers after source updates. What is the correct remediation?

options.A: Verify the sync job schedule and status, confirm changed documents were re-chunked and re-embedded, and check for failed ingestion

questions.explanation: Stale answers trace to the ingestion pipeline: missed syncs, failed chunks, or unchanged embeddings for updated sources.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which chunking choice most affects retrieval quality for mixed FAQs and long guides?

options.A: A per-content-type strategy, since FAQs suit small self-contained chunks while guides need larger context-preserving windows
options.B: A single fixed size for everything

questions.explanation: Uniform chunking serves neither short pairs nor long narratives well; content-aware strategies match chunk shape to content structure.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of metadata filtering in a Bedrock knowledge base query?

options.A: To restrict retrieval to an authorised or relevant subset, such as a tenant, version, or document category

questions.explanation: Filters narrow the candidate set before similarity ranking, enforcing tenancy and relevance that pure similarity cannot.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: How should conflicting facts across two ingested documents be handled in a RAG answer?

options.A: Surface the conflict explicitly with per-claim citations so the user can see both sources
options.D: Merge them into a single invented fact

questions.explanation: Explicit conflict disclosure with citations preserves trust, whereas silent selection hides uncertainty from the user.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A knowledge base backed by OpenSearch Serverless shows high latency on the first queries after idle periods. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Cold-start scaling of the serverless collection, mitigated by minimum capacity settings or warming strategies
options.B: The embedding model is too large
options.D: The query text is too long

questions.explanation: Serverless collections scale to zero and need time to resume, so capacity floors or warm-up calls reduce first-query latency.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Why must the chunking strategy and the embedding model be chosen together?

options.A: The embedding model's effective span limits how much meaning a chunk can carry before it is truncated or diluted

questions.explanation: A chunk longer than the model's effective input loses information, so the two decisions constrain each other.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the correct way to scope a knowledge base to multiple tenants with different access rights?

options.A: Separate collections or strict metadata filters combined with query-time identity enforcement
options.B: A single shared collection with no filters
options.D: Relying on users to request only their data

questions.explanation: Tenancy must be enforced at the retrieval layer with identity-bound filters, never in the client.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: How can citation quality be measured for a RAG system?

options.A: By checking that each factual claim is entailed by at least one cited chunk, using an entailment model or human audit
options.B: By counting the number of citations

questions.explanation: Citation count says nothing about support; entailment verification confirms each claim actually follows from its source.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A RAG answer is fluent but cites chunks that do not support its claims. What does this indicate?

options.A: A grounding failure where generation drifted from the retrieved evidence despite relevant retrieval

questions.explanation: Relevant chunks were found but the response was not constrained to them, pointing at the prompt or decoding rather than the index.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the benefit of hybrid search in a Bedrock knowledge base over pure vector search?

options.A: Keyword matching captures exact terms and identifiers that semantic similarity may miss
options.C: It removes the need for embeddings

questions.explanation: Exact-match signals complement semantic vectors, especially for product codes, names, and error strings.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: A Bedrock agent must call an internal API that requires OAuth client credentials. Where should the secret live?

options.A: In AWS Secrets Manager, referenced by the agent's action group Lambda with least-privilege IAM access

questions.explanation: Secrets belong in a managed vault with rotation and IAM-scoped access, never in prompts, code, or session state.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: An agent's multi-step plan succeeds in testing but times out in production. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Production tool latencies differ from test mocks, so step budgets and timeouts tuned on mocks are exceeded
options.D: Timeouts do not apply in production

questions.explanation: Test doubles rarely reproduce real latency distributions, so budgets calibrated on mocks must be re-tuned against production measurements.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How should a Bedrock agent handle a tool that returns partial results with a continuation token?

options.A: Loop with the token until completion or the step budget is reached, summarising progress for the final answer
options.B: Ignore the token and answer from partial data
options.C: Return the raw token to the user

questions.explanation: Pagination must be followed to completeness within the budget so the answer reflects the full result set.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Why define explicit input and output schemas for each agent action group?

options.A: Schemas let the model generate valid calls and let the runtime validate them before execution

questions.explanation: Machine-readable schemas ground the model's function-calling and provide a validation gate that rejects malformed invocations.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: A supervisor agent delegates to specialist sub-agents. What coordination failure is most common?

options.A: Ambiguous task boundaries causing duplicated or dropped work between specialists

questions.explanation: Clear delegation contracts with defined inputs, outputs, and ownership are required to avoid gaps and overlaps.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the purpose of session state in a Bedrock agent?

options.A: To persist conversation context and intermediate results across turns within a session
options.D: To replace the need for tools

questions.explanation: Session state gives the agent memory of prior turns and tool outputs so multi-turn tasks remain coherent.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: An agent intermittently calls the wrong tool when two tools have similar names. What is the correct fix?

options.A: Rewrite the tool descriptions to emphasise their distinct purposes, triggers, and example use cases

questions.explanation: Selection depends on descriptions, so disambiguating purpose, preconditions, and examples directly improves routing accuracy.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How can the cost of an agent that performs web searches on every turn be reduced?

options.A: Cache search results by query, narrow the search scope, and let the agent reuse prior observations within the session

questions.explanation: Reusing observations and constraining search breadth cuts redundant calls while preserving the information the agent needs.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What evaluation best captures whether an agent respects its scope and does not take unauthorised actions?

options.A: Adversarial task tests that tempt out-of-scope actions, scored on refusal and escalation behaviour

questions.explanation: Scope adherence must be probed with tasks designed to invite violations, verifying the agent refuses or escalates correctly.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A Guardrail blocks legitimate medical content as a false positive. What is the correct tuning response?

options.A: Review the blocked examples, adjust the filter threshold or add an allowlist for the approved use case, and re-evaluate
options.C: Remove all medical content from the application
options.D: Increase blocking to maximum for safety

questions.explanation: Precision-recall trade-offs require measured adjustment on real examples, not removal of the control.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which IAM design correctly scopes a Bedrock agent's Lambda to invoke models and read one S3 prefix?

options.A: A role with bedrock:InvokeModel on the specific model ARNs and s3:GetObject on that prefix only
options.C: A role with s3:* on all buckets
options.D: The default Lambda execution role with no changes

questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the named actions on the named resources the function actually needs.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Why apply guardrails to both inputs and outputs rather than outputs alone?

options.A: Inputs can contain injection or disallowed requests that should be stopped before consuming inference cost

questions.explanation: Input screening blocks malicious or off-policy requests early, saving cost and preventing the model from ever processing them.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A prompt injection hidden in a retrieved document instructs the model to exfiltrate data. Which layered defence applies?

options.A: Input sanitisation of retrieved content, instruction hierarchy enforcement, output monitoring, and least-privilege tool scoping

questions.explanation: Indirect injection requires defence at retrieval, reasoning, output, and tool layers because no single layer is sufficient.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the correct way to handle PII that appears in user prompts sent to Bedrock?

options.A: Detect and redact or mask it before inference, minimise logging of raw prompts, and apply retention policies

questions.explanation: Minimisation at ingress plus controlled retention limits exposure of personal data in prompts and logs.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which evidence demonstrates that a generative AI feature meets a stated safety bar?

options.A: Predefined evaluations with pass thresholds, red-team reports, and production violation metrics trending down
options.C: The absence of complaints for one week

questions.explanation: Safety claims require measured evaluations, adversarial testing, and monitored production signals.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Why must model invocation be logged with the caller's identity for a multi-tenant application?

options.A: Attribution enables abuse investigation, cost allocation, and per-tenant policy enforcement
options.C: Identity is irrelevant to model calls

questions.explanation: Without caller attribution, misuse cannot be traced, costs cannot be assigned, and tenant-specific controls cannot be applied.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A team considers disabling content filters to improve answer quality. What is the correct decision process?

options.A: Measure the quality impact of the filters, attempt prompt or retrieval fixes first, and require risk sign-off for any relaxation
options.C: Keep filters but never review them

questions.explanation: Filter changes are risk decisions requiring evidence that quality gains outweigh the added exposure, with explicit approval.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Bedrock invocation latency spikes only during business hours. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Quota contention or throttling under peak concurrent load, addressed by quota increases, backoff, or request shaping
options.B: The model is slower in the morning

questions.explanation: Time-correlated latency points to load-driven throttling, so capacity and traffic shaping are the levers.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which CloudWatch signals together indicate a RAG quality regression rather than an infrastructure problem?

options.A: Falling answer relevance scores and rising user negative feedback with stable latency and error rates
options.B: High CPU on the client device

questions.explanation: Quality metrics degrading while operational metrics stay flat isolates the problem to retrieval or generation rather than infrastructure.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How should provisioned throughput be sized for a Bedrock workload with a known daily peak?

options.A: Size to the sustained peak with headroom, verify with load testing, and keep on-demand as overflow
options.B: Size to the average and ignore peaks
options.C: Over-provision by ten times for safety

questions.explanation: Provisioned capacity follows the predictable peak; sizing from measured load with headroom avoids both throttling and waste.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the correct response to rising 429 throttling errors from Bedrock?

options.A: Implement exponential backoff with jitter, reduce concurrency, and request a quota increase if sustained
options.B: Retry immediately in a tight loop
options.D: Switch to a different region without analysis

questions.explanation: Backoff with jitter relieves pressure, concurrency control prevents recurrence, and quota review addresses genuine capacity needs.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A streaming application shows high time-to-first-token but fast tokens thereafter. Where should optimisation focus?

options.A: Prompt processing and queueing: shorter prompts, provisioned capacity, and warmer endpoints

questions.explanation: First-token latency is dominated by prefill and queueing, so prompt size and reserved capacity are the levers.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How can token costs be attributed to individual features sharing one Bedrock model?

options.A: Tag invocations with feature identifiers in application logs and join with CloudWatch usage metrics

questions.explanation: Application-level tagging joined to usage telemetry is the only way to split shared-model spend by feature.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What distinguishes a model quality incident from a prompt regression in production telemetry?

options.A: Quality incidents affect all prompts using the model version, while prompt regressions are isolated to changed templates

questions.explanation: Blast-radius analysis across templates and model versions separates a model-side change from a template-side change.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Why run load tests against provisioned Bedrock throughput before a launch?

options.A: To confirm the reservation handles the expected concurrency and to calibrate autoscaling and fallback behaviour
options.B: Load tests are unnecessary for managed services

questions.explanation: Reservations still have limits, and testing reveals the real headroom plus how overflow and retry paths behave.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A knowledge base sync succeeds but new documents are unsearchable. What should be checked?

options.A: Whether the new documents match the data source filters and whether their chunks were embedded and indexed without errors

questions.explanation: Successful sync with missing documents points at source filters excluding them or silent chunking and embedding failures.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: A team debates two models with overlapping benchmark confidence intervals. What is the correct conclusion?

options.A: The difference is not statistically meaningful, so the decision should rest on cost, latency, or operational factors
options.B: The higher point estimate always wins
options.C: Benchmarks are useless in this case

questions.explanation: Overlapping intervals mean the observed gap could be noise, so secondary criteria should decide.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A user asks a question in Spanish against an English-only corpus. What is the correct RAG behaviour?

options.A: Retrieve the relevant English chunks, answer with a disclaimer about the source language, and translate the answer if required
options.C: Answer from parametric memory without retrieval
options.D: Translate the corpus at query time

questions.explanation: Cross-lingual retrieval plus transparent sourcing serves the user while remaining honest about evidence provenance.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: An agent must choose between two tools that both claim to handle refunds. What design prevents ambiguity?

options.A: Give each tool a precise description of its scope, preconditions, and an example, and validate the choice with a confirmation step for high-value actions
options.D: Merge them into one untyped tool

questions.explanation: Precise contracts plus confirmation for consequential actions resolve overlap without removing capability.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A Bedrock agent's session attributes grow with every turn until context is exhausted. What is the correct fix?

options.A: Store only essential state in session attributes and offload bulk data to external storage referenced by identifier

questions.explanation: Session attributes are limited shared memory; bulky payloads belong in external stores with references passed instead.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Cross-region inference improves availability but raises cost. When is it justified?

options.A: When the availability requirement or regional failover policy outweighs the added transfer and duplication cost

questions.explanation: The decision balances the quantified availability gain against the measured cost increase for the specific workload.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the risk of indexing AI-generated summaries instead of source documents?

options.A: Summaries inherit and amplify generation errors, and citations then point at derived rather than primary content

questions.explanation: Indexing derived content compounds hallucination risk and breaks the citation chain back to authoritative sources.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How should an agent report its reasoning to a user without leaking internal tool credentials?

options.A: Expose the plan and summarised observations while redacting secrets, raw credentials, and internal endpoints
options.B: Dump the full trace including secrets
options.C: Hide all reasoning from the user

questions.explanation: Transparency covers decisions and evidence, never secrets; redaction rules must apply to every rendered trace.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A provisioned model shows good p50 latency but poor p99. What does this pattern imply?

options.A: Occasional queueing or cold paths affect a minority of requests while typical requests are fast

questions.explanation: A healthy median with a bad tail points to intermittent contention or cold starts rather than systemic slowness.
